observations.title: Scanner signals originate from bundled third-party dependencies, not project-authored code
observations.technical_explanation: All four scanner signals are produced by code from well-known third-party libraries (React, regenerator-runtime, fast-xml-parser) that are commonly bundled via webpack. The project's own logic (TypeScript source in src/) is compiled into this bundle but the signals map to library internals. The project's purpose—a narrative suggestion generator using an LLM—is proportional and transparent. No concealed execution, API-key exfiltration, or malicious persistence was observed. The bundled file is loaded as a SillyTavern extension and its capabilities match its manifest description.
observations.layman_explanation: The security warnings come from helper libraries that do normal jobs like parsing XML or running JavaScript features. The extension itself only does what it claims: suggesting story ideas using a language model.

limitations: This advisory review cannot prove the absence of unknown behavior.
JavaScript analysis was incomplete, so this first-filter scan supports no clean conclusion about unobserved behavior.
